steps.title: Calculate lentiviral particle requirements
steps.instruction: Determine the total transducing units (TU) needed per well using the desired multiplicity of infection (MOI) and the lentiviral titer supplied on the certificate of analysis (e.g., 1 × 10⁷ TU/mL). Compute particles per well as Total TU ÷ titer; for this protocol an MOI of 20 was used.

substeps.instruction: Total TU = Number of particles per well × MOI.
Number of particles per well = Total TU ÷ lentiviral titer (TU/mL).

steps.title: Gather required lentiviral reagents
steps.instruction: Collect the following lentiviral particles and control reagents before starting the transfection.

substeps.instruction: MISSION shRNA lentiviral transduction particles (TSC2; TRCN0000010454; Millipore Sigma, SHCLNV).
MISSION pLKO.1‑puro‑CMV‑tGFP positive‑control particles (Millipore Sigma, SHC003V).
MISSION pLKO.1‑puro non‑target shRNA control particles (Millipore Sigma, SHC016V).

steps.title: Prepare western lysis buffer (500 µL)
steps.instruction: Mix the components on ice to obtain 500 µL of lysis buffer for protein extraction.

substeps.instruction: Add 485 µL RIPA lysis and extraction buffer (97%).
Add 5 µL PMSF (1 mM final).
Add 5 µL protease inhibitor cocktail set III (1 % final).
Add 5 µL phosphatase inhibitor cocktail set II (1 % final).
Bring volume to 500 µL with nuclease‑free water if needed (total already 500 µL).
Store at 4 °C; use within 4 h.

steps.title: Prepare western transfer buffer (1 L, pH 8.3)
steps.instruction: Combine the listed reagents to make 1 L of transfer buffer for gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 mL 10× Tris/glycine/SDS (1× final).
Add 100 mL methanol (10 % final).
Add 800 mL Milli‑Q water (80 % final).
Adjust pH to 8.3 if necessary.
Store at 4 °C for up to 1 year; buffer can be reused 3–4 times.

steps.title: Prepare TBST and BSA/milk blocking buffers
steps.instruction: Make 1 L of TBST, then add BSA or non‑fat milk to create blocking solutions.

substeps.instruction: TBST: Mix 100 mL 10× TBS, 1 mL Tween‑20 (10 % v/v), and 899 mL Milli‑Q water; store at 20‑22 °C for up to 4 months.
TBST + 3 % BSA: Dissolve 1.5 g BSA in 1 L TBST; store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
TBST + 5 % non‑fat milk: Dissolve 2.5 g milk powder in 1 L TBST; store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Reconstitute viability dye and make PBS‑1% BSA
steps.instruction: Prepare the LIVE/DEAD Fixable Red dye and a PBS solution containing 1 % BSA for staining.

substeps.instruction: Thaw component A (red fluorescent reactive dye) and component B (anhydrous DMSO) from the LIVE/DEAD kit at 20‑22 °C.
Add 50 µL DMSO to the vial of red dye, mix thoroughly until fully dissolved.
Aliquot the reconstituted dye if desired; store at –80 °C for up to 3 months (use within a few hours of preparation).
Prepare 10 mL PBS‑1 % BSA by adding 0.10 g BSA to 10 mL PBS; keep on ice.

steps.title: Dissociate enteroids to single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension from transfected enteroids cultured in 96‑well plates.

substeps.instruction: Warm TrypLE Express to 37 °C in a water or bead bath.
Aspirate media from each well of the 96‑well plate.
Add 200 µL pre‑warmed TrypLE Express to each well.
Mechanically disrupt the Matrigel sandwich by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Incubate plate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Add 100 µL ice‑cold PBS to each well to dilute TrypLE.
Pipette up and down 10–20 times to further dissociate cells.
Transfer the contents of each treatment group into a 5 mL polypropylene round‑bottom tube (repeat for all groups).
Centrifuge tubes at 400 × g, 4 °C for 5 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS, centrifuge again (400 × g, 4 °C, 5 min).
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 500 µL PBS.
Count cells using a Countess 3 or hemocytometer; ensure ≥1 × 10⁵ cells per condition for flow cytometry.

steps.title: Stain cells for viability and fix
steps.instruction: Label live/dead cells with the amino‑reactive dye, fix, and prepare for flow analysis.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the 5 mL tubes at 400 × g, 4 °C for 5 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold PBS (avoid BSA‑containing buffers for this step).
Add 1 µL reconstituted red dye to each tube (using a 2 µL pipette with 10 µL tips); mix gently.
Incubate tubes in the dark at 20‑22 °C for 30 min.
Centrifuge again (400 × g, 4 °C, 5 min) and wash cells with 1 mL PBS; repeat wash.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL 10 % neutral buffered formalin (NBF); incubate in the dark at 20‑22 °C for 15 min.
Centrifuge (400 × g, 4 °C, 5 min) and wash with 1 mL ice‑cold PBS containing 1 % BSA; repeat wash.
Keep tubes on ice; fixed, stained cells may be stored in the dark at 4 °C for up to 2 h.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run the stained cells on a flow cytometer, set compensation, and collect data for transduction efficiency and viability.

substeps.instruction: Power on the BD Accuri C6 Plus (or equivalent) and perform manufacturer‑recommended quality control.
Load BrightComp eBeads GFP Compensation Bead Kit (or GFP‑expressing cells) to establish compensation settings for GFP (FITC) and the red viability channel (PE).
Place an empty well on the 96‑well plate grid and assign a sample name.
Set acquisition parameters: 10 000 events per sample, slow fluidics rate (14 µL/min), FSC threshold 200 000–500 000, secondary threshold at 640 nm to exclude red autofluorescence.
Collect GFP (FL1, 530/30) and viability dye (FL3, >670 nm) signals; display data on logarithmic scales.
Load each sample (optionally filter through a 37 µm cell strainer) and run; save the workspace after each run.
Gate sequentially: FSC vs. SSC to select single cells, then PE vs. FITC to identify live (low PE) and transfected (high FITC) populations.
Export plots and raw .fsc files for downstream analysis.

description: The protocol below describes the lentiviral transfection of human preterm ileal enteroids with the objective of increasing mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) activation through gene knockdown of its negative regulator, tuberous sclerosis complex 2 (TSC2).1 Enteroids provide a highly translational model of the human intestine.2,3,4 While various protocols have been described to genetically modify enteroids,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13 technical challenges have often limited efficacy of genetic manipulation in these cultures.14,15,16 Here, we introduce a procedure predicated upon methodology from Maru et al.17 This protocol incorporates a puromycin selection cytotoxicity trial, preparation of enteroid media, lentiviral transfection of enteroids, and flow cytometry, electrophoresis, western blotting, and densitometry to assess transfection outcomes. As this protocol involves the use of lentiviral particles, all steps are performed within a type II biological safety cabinet in a biological safety level 2 (BSL2) laboratory.
